Holubyne Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakarpattia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. The first Jews arrived in Holubyne in the mid-18th century, with a single family recorded in 1768; the population grew to 121 (15.6 percent) by 1880 and 186 by 1921, engaged as tradesmen, artisans, farmers, and flour mill operators. Following the March 1939 Hungarian occupation, Jews were persecuted and forced out of their occupations; the population reached 209 by 1941, with many drafted into forced labor battalions or sent to the Eastern Front, where most perished. In August 1941, Jews without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to German-occupied Kamianets-Podilskyi and shot, and the remaining Jews of Holubyne were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944.
